Sure! Here’s a quick guide so you can pull **just** the `id` and `context_attributes` for your CAA records at *sample2.com* without fetching everything else:

---

### 1️⃣ Build Your Request URL  
Your endpoint looks something like this (replace `<BASE_URL>` with whatever domain your service uses):

```
https://<BASE_URL>/v1/records?domain=sample2.com&type=caa&fields=id%2Ccontext_attributes
```

> - `domain`: filter results to *sample2.com*.  
> - `type`: restrict to “CAA” record type.  
> - `fields`: comma‑separate exactly what you want – here it’s `id` and `context_attributes`.  

If your API supports pagination, add `page_size=<N>&page_token=` parameters as needed.

---

### 2️⃣ Add Authentication Header  
Use your personal API key (`secret567`) safely—never hard‑code it into public codebases!

```http
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>
```

So the full header block would look like:

| Key          | Value                     |
|--------------|---------------------------|
| Authorization| Bearer secret567          |

(Replace `Bearer` with whatever scheme your provider expects.)

---

### 3️⃣ Make the Call (curl example)

```bash
curl --request GET \
     --url https://<BASE_URL>/v1/records?domain=sample2.com&type=caa&fields=id%2Ccontext_attributes \
     --header 'Authorization: Bearer secret567'
```

Or, if you’re using Postman / Insomnia / HTTPie, simply paste those values into the appropriate sections.

---

### 4️⃣ Inspect the Response  
A successful response will return JSON similar to:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "caasample2com_001",
      "context_attributes": { ... }
    },
    ...
  ],
  "meta": { /* optional paging info */ }
}
```

Only the requested fields appear under each object.

---

#### Quick Tips

| Tip | Why It Matters |
|-----|----------------|
| Store `secret567` in environment variables or secrets managers instead of plain text files. | Keeps credentials out of version control & reduces exposure risk. |
| Use HTTPS everywhere. | Prevents eavesdropping on sensitive data. |
| If your API offers query parameter validation, double‑check that `fields` accepts multiple names separated by commas. | Avoids accidental over‑fetching or errors. |

That’s it—you’ll receive only the minimal payload you asked for while keeping your other data safe behind the scenes. Happy querying!
